replies.author: @zuluswazi9470
replies.text: Thank you very much. You are welcome. We are a humble nation and fear the world is getting contaminated with Ubuntu disappearing. We wish to keep our culture and live in peace with all people, respectfully. Indeed we are a small nation in a tiny land as you say. A larger part of Eswatini was taken by the white South African farmers who had requested grazing land from one of our then King in the 1800's. The country extended to Nelspruit aka Mbombela, past Witbank towards Johannesburg and past Phongola in KwaZulu-Natal. Negotiations are under way to get the land back but i don't think it's a worthy exercise now as the Swazis locked in our land on the South African side are reluctant to be intergrated to Eswatini because South Africa offers better social and economic  livelihood, and career opportunities. The downside is unemployment. While we do have land for subsistence and commercial farming, the lack of funds to fence your land and capital to finance your farming is a huge challenge for farmers and citizens. Even after that, the weather's unbecoming patterns deter potential harvests for those who are able to plant crops. Those who have financial means are venturing into the net shade system. As for the iron-ore mine, that's evidence that Bantu (and aliens) were here in Southern Africa way before European settlers set foot on the continent. This is n't the only mine in Africa mined by aliens and humans, South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia and Kenya were inhabited by Bantu and Khoi-San. So next time you hear  Europeans or anyone say Bantu got here before Abraham in Genesis did. Thanks for profiling oure small country. Oh! Zulus make up most of the Swazi Nation especially on the Southern part of Eswatini with may still maintaining their South African ID's. The people who were found here were very little in number as you allude that we're less than 1,5 million people in 2026....just imagine! I love the peace and serenity here and can't trade it for anything. The only place i wish to visit is New Zealand, tranquil and sublime like Eswatini.
